preserved_details.actor: Temple precinct accounting clerk or administrator
preserved_details.documented_action: Modeling in wet clay, incising strokes, counting, sorting by commodity type, storing in groups
preserved_details.label: Geometric clay tokens in Late Uruk administrative levels
limitations: Contexts in early excavations often disturbed; Neolithic antecedents vary in function and do not represent a single unified code across 5000 years
preserved_details.measurement: 1 to 3 cm in diameter / height
preserved_details.object_or_trace: Small unbaked or lightly fired clay geometric shapes (spheres, cones, disks, cylinders), some plain and some incised with geometric marks
preserved_details.physical_description: Hand-modeled clay objects generally between 1 and 3 cm in dimension, with matte earthen surface and fingernail or stylus incisions
preserved_details.representativeness: standard administrative material in late prehistoric southern Mesopotamia

preserved_details.actor: Institutional storehouse official and transacting parties
preserved_details.documented_action: Enclosing tokens inside wet clay envelope, pressing tokens onto exterior surface to record quantity, rolling cylinder seal across exterior to guarantee integrity, drying
explicit_sequence: deposit tokens in hollow clay ball
press tokens into wet exterior wall
preserved_details.label: Hollow clay bulla (envelope) with enclosed tokens and exterior impressions
limitations: Breakable verification device; once opened to inspect contents, the sealed envelope is permanently destroyed
preserved_details.measurement: 5 to 7 cm diameter, wall thickness 1 to 1.5 cm
preserved_details.object_or_trace: Globular hollow clay sphere sealed shut while moist, containing tokens inside and displaying surface impressions of those tokens and cylinder seals on the outside
preserved_details.physical_description: Spherical to ovoid clay ball 5 to 7 cm across, with thick walls, hollow core, and overlapping impressed marks and rolled figurative seal impressions
preserved_details.representativeness: widespread verification practice in greater Uruk sphere before flat numerical tablets

preserved_details.actor: Authorized institutional agent or witness
preserved_details.documented_action: Rolling engraved cylinder across wet clay surface of bullae, jar stoppers, or numerical tablets to leave continuous raised impression
preserved_details.label: Cylinder seal and impressed clay rollings
limitations: Identifies institutional authority or witness presence, not spoken syntax or linguistic phonology
preserved_details.measurement: length 2–5 cm, diameter 1–2.5 cm
preserved_details.object_or_trace: Carved hard stone cylinder (limestone, lapis, calcite) engraved with negative relief of captive processions, animal herds, or administrative activities
preserved_details.physical_description: Perforated stone cylinder 2 to 5 cm in length, diameter 1 to 2.5 cm, engraved with micro-relief scenes
preserved_details.representativeness: universal authentication device across administrative Mesopotamia and Elam
preserved_details.time: Middle to Late Uruk period (ca. 3500–3100 BCE)

preserved_details.actor: Storehouse accountant
preserved_details.documented_action: Shaping lump of clay into flattened pillow, pressing blunt round end of reed or wood stylus perpendicularly or at an angle to create numerical impressions, rolling seal across reverse
explicit_sequence: impress round stylus for large units
impress oblique stylus for small units
preserved_details.label: Solid numerical tablet with stylus impressions
limitations: Records quantities and transaction categories without specifying full grammatical sentences or spoken words
preserved_details.measurement: 4 to 6 cm length, 3 to 5 cm width, 1.5 to 2.5 cm thickness
preserved_details.object_or_trace: Cushion-shaped clay tablet bearing impressed circular, semi-circular, and stroke-shaped numerical signs without pictographic script signs
preserved_details.physical_description: Thick rounded rectangular clay tablet, roughly palm-sized, with distinct deep round depressions and oblique circular cups
preserved_details.representativeness: direct material predecessor and contemporary companion to pictographic proto-cuneiform tablets
preserved_details.time: Late Uruk period, Uruk V to early IV (ca. 3300–3200 BCE)

preserved_details.actor: Trained archaic scribe (dubsar-precursor) and temple administrator
preserved_details.documented_action: Scoring dividing lines into soft clay with pointed stylus, pressing numerical punches, incising ideographic drawings (heads, grain sheaves, vessels, animals), totaling sums on reverse
explicit_sequence: pat wet clay into rectangular tablet
press numerical notations in each compartment
draw pictographic commodity signs beside numbers
preserved_details.label: Archaic proto-cuneiform administrative account (Uruk IV)
limitations: Texts are ledger-style administrative allocations; do not record running continuous spoken discourse, poetry, or historical narrative
preserved_details.measurement: 5 to 8 cm length, 4 to 7 cm width, 1.5 to 2 cm thickness
preserved_details.object_or_trace: Clay tablet ruled into compartments (cases), combining impressed numerical notations with incised pictographic signs representing commodities, persons, and institutions
preserved_details.physical_description: Convex clay tablet 5 to 8 cm square, light buff or greyish clay, clearly divided by incision lines with deeply impressed numerals and thin drawn pictographs
preserved_details.representativeness: canonical early Uruk IV administrative accounting tablet

preserved_details.actor: Scribe or record maker
preserved_details.documented_action: Cutting reed from marshland, shaping tip with blade, pressing into wet clay at varying angles, drawing curved pictographic outlines
preserved_details.label: Pointed and round-ended reed styluses
limitations: Organic material rarely preserved directly in archaeological record; tool morphology reconstructed from impressions and incisions in clay
preserved_details.measurement: 10–15 cm length, 0.5–0.8 cm diameter
preserved_details.object_or_trace: Cut marsh reed (Phragmites australis) stalks with carved pointed end for incising curved lines and blunt rounded/semi-circular ends for numerical punches
preserved_details.physical_description: Short slender reed stalk 10 to 15 cm long, smooth exterior siliceous rind, cut diagonally and rounded on opposite ends
preserved_details.place: Southern Mesopotamian riverine and marsh landscape
preserved_details.representativeness: universal primary writing implement of early Mesopotamia

preserved_details.actor: Storeroom keeper and inspecting officer
preserved_details.documented_action: Binding door or jar with twisted reed/flax cord, applying moist clay pat over knot, rolling cylinder seal to lock closure, breaking clay seal upon authorized opening
preserved_details.label: Administrative sealing assemblage on clay jar stoppers and door pegs
limitations: Documents physical custody and unauthorized entry prevention, not textual content
preserved_details.measurement: 3 to 8 cm width
preserved_details.object_or_trace: Clay sealings (cretulae) pressed over woven reed mats, jar cloth covers, wooden pegs inserted into storeroom walls, with cord impressions on underside and seal rollings on top
preserved_details.physical_description: Irregular lumps of clay bearing negative impressions of rope, wood pegs, or coarse cloth on interior face and multiple seal rollings on exterior
preserved_details.representativeness: standard administrative locking and witnessing practice preceding and accompanying written accounts

preserved_details.actor: Ration distribution foreman, temple dependent laborers, grain storekeepers
preserved_details.documented_action: Measuring standardized portions of barley or emmer wheat into coarse standardized bowls, tallying recipients against inscribed tablet cases, recording distributed amounts
explicit_sequence: scoop grain into standardized bevel-rimmed bowl
tally remaining grain balance on tablet reverse
preserved_details.label: Institutional ration accounting and disbursement procedure

preserved_details.representativeness: most abundant ceramic marker of Uruk institutional expansion and organized redistribution

record.statement: The direct token→tablet→writing sequence is too linear; seals, iconography, bullae, numerical tablets and institutional practice formed a parallel ecology.

record.counterevidence: Named agents, commodities, metrology and document structure sometimes narrow the transaction, but sign readings and institutional context remain incomplete.
record.statement: The preserved proto-cuneiform corpus can distinguish accounting contexts more securely than it can distinguish market exchange from tax, tribute or redistribution.

preserved_details.measurement: length 2–5 cm, diameter 1–2.5 cm
preserved_details.object_or_trace: Carved hard stone cylinder (limestone, lapis, calcite) engraved with negative relief of captive processions, animal herds, or administrative activities
preserved_details.physical_description: Perforated stone cylinder 2 to 5 cm in length, diameter 1 to 2.5 cm, engraved with micro-relief scenes
preserved_details.representativeness: universal authentication device across administrative Mesopotamia and Elam
preserved_details.time: Middle to Late Uruk period (ca. 3500–3100 BCE)

preserved_details.actor: Storeroom keeper and inspecting officer
preserved_details.documented_action: Binding door or jar with twisted reed/flax cord, applying moist clay pat over knot, rolling cylinder seal to lock closure, breaking clay seal upon authorized opening
preserved_details.label: Administrative sealing assemblage on clay jar stoppers and door pegs
limitations: Documents physical custody and unauthorized entry prevention, not textual content
preserved_details.measurement: 3 to 8 cm width
preserved_details.object_or_trace: Clay sealings (cretulae) pressed over woven reed mats, jar cloth covers, wooden pegs inserted into storeroom walls, with cord impressions on underside and seal rollings on top
preserved_details.physical_description: Irregular lumps of clay bearing negative impressions of rope, wood pegs, or coarse cloth on interior face and multiple seal rollings on exterior
preserved_details.representativeness: standard administrative locking and witnessing practice preceding and accompanying written accounts
